supported_claim: Partial Cytoland fine-tuning improves over frozen DINOv2 in all six reporters.
evidence: Mean paired delta 0.0785; reporter-hierarchical 95% CI 0.0328 to 0.1300; 6/6 positive.
not_supported: This does not show that the fine-tuned encoder is optimal.
positive_interpretation: Domain adaptation recovers information absent from a generic frozen image representation.
negative_interpretation: A smaller or null effect in a larger reporter panel would restrict the claim to this pilot.

supported_claim: Partial fine-tuning does not clearly improve over frozen Cytoland.
evidence: Mean paired delta 0.0187; 95% CI -0.0076 to 0.0502; 4/6 positive.
not_supported: The panel cannot claim a reliable fine-tuning advantage over Cytoland.
positive_interpretation: Any gain over the domain-specific frozen encoder is modest.
negative_interpretation: The compatible interval includes no gain and should be reported as inconclusive.

supported_claim: The official 172D morphology baseline remains stronger than partial Cytoland fine-tuning in this pilot.
evidence: Mean paired delta -0.1266; 95% CI -0.1881 to -0.0657; 0/6 positive.
not_supported: This is not evidence that raw phase images lack recoverable information or that no image model can close the gap.
positive_interpretation: The tested image representations do not yet replace the engineered morphology features.
negative_interpretation: The gap motivates representation work but is not part of the measurement-sufficiency causal claim.
